top.headline: Homeland Security Raids Rep. Ilhan Omar's Residence
top.blurb: Homeland Security Investigations agents searched Rep. Ilhan Omar's Washington home on a Justice Department warrant tied to a probe into immigration paperwork her late father filed when she was a child. The raid came about three weeks before the midterms, a window when DOJ policy usually pauses such actions; Omar calls it an attempt to weaponize federal law enforcement against a political opponent.

top.headline: DOJ Opens Antitrust Probe Into Five TV Networks Over Suspended Trump Pool Coverage
top.blurb: The Justice Department opened an antitrust investigation into ABC, CBS, CNN, NBC and Fox News over their brief, coordinated halt to White House pool coverage after Trump barred CNN, Politico and MS NOW from the briefing room. DOJ says a 'group boycott among competitors' can violate the Sherman Act; press-freedom groups call the probe itself an attempt to intimidate journalists.

more.headline: Mamdani Orders First NYPD Use-of-Force Review in a Decade
more.blurb: New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani ordered the city's first review of NYPD use-of-force policies in a decade, his office announced Monday.

top.headline: Rahul Gandhi and INDIA Bloc Leaders Move Supreme Court Against Voter-Roll Purge
top.blurb: Rahul Gandhi and ten other INDIA bloc leaders petitioned the Supreme Court against the Election Commission's voter-roll revision after Chief Justice Surya Kant declined to meet them, seeking an independent audit of voter deletions and a suspension of the exercise. The filing came amid nationwide protests demanding CEC Gyanesh Kumar's resignation over revelations that two fellow commissioners had objected to SIR decisions 14 times.

top.headline: Houthi Missiles Target Riyadh for a Third Day as Saudi Arabia Shuts Its Main Airport
top.blurb: The Saudi-led coalition said it intercepted missiles aimed at Riyadh and Khamis Mushait as Houthi attacks on Saudi airports entered a third day, prompting King Khalid International to stay closed until Saturday and airlines including Lufthansa to cancel flights through October 16. Trump called the Houthis 'misbehaving very badly' but gave no sign the US would join the Saudi-led campaign.

top.headline: Zelenskyy Accuses Russia of Violating Trump's 'Energy Ceasefire' Within a Day
top.blurb: A day after Trump announced an energy ceasefire between Russia and Ukraine, Zelenskyy said Russian strikes hit six Ukrainian energy facilities, accusing Moscow of violating a truce it never confirmed agreeing to. The Kremlin separately rejected Zelenskyy's offer to hold wartime elections in exchange for a 60-day truce.

top.headline: Australia Six Wickets From Test Win in Durban as Smith's Head Knock Overshadows the Chase
top.blurb: Australia need six more wickets to win the first Test in Durban after Matthew Renshaw's 82 helped set South Africa a target of 421, with the tourists taking four wickets in a one-sided final session. The bigger concern was vice-captain Steve Smith, hit on the head by an Anrich Nortje bouncer and held back from fielding pending a concussion assessment.

top.headline: Mahershala Ali on Still Being Hungry as an Actor: 'Let's Fail on Camera Until We Find It'
top.blurb: In a Fresh Air conversation tied to his new film about a hit man left to raise his kids alone, Mahershala Ali tells Tonya Mosley that two decades and two Oscars in, he still chases roles that scare him and would rather risk failing on camera than play it safe.

bengal.headline: Kolkata Police Summon CPI(M)'s Bikash Ranjan Bhattacharya Over 'Hindutva Goons' Remark
bengal.blurb: Days after his Kolkata home was attacked, police summoned CPI(M) leader Bikash Ranjan Bhattacharya to two stations over a social-media post blaming 'Hindutva goons.'

travel.headline: Discover Berlin's Best Neighborhoods
travel.blurb: Lonely Planet's guide to Berlin sorts six neighborhoods by traveler type, from Mitte's museums and history to Friedrichshain-Kreuzberg's nightlife and Prenzlauer Berg's quieter, art-filled streets.

travel.headline: A Century-Old Fossil Skull Found in the Sphinx's Stone Turns Out to Be a New Crocodile Species
travel.blurb: A fossil crocodilian skull pulled from the same Egyptian limestone used to build the Great Sphinx a century ago has now been identified as a previously unknown species.

happy.headline: Scientists Took a Cheek Swab From the World's Oldest Tortoise. His DNA Could Reveal Hints to Longevity
happy.blurb: Jonathan, a roughly 194-year-old tortoise on St. Helena, gave up a cheek swab for a new genetic study hunting for the secrets behind a life that has outlasted his species' average by over a century.

tech_top.headline: Meta Releases Its First Frontier AI Model, Muse Wonder
tech_top.blurb: Meta's Superintelligence Lab released Muse Wonder and a subscriber-only Muse Wonder Full, priced at $4 per million input tokens and $20 per million output tokens through the Meta Model API, marking the company's first model pitched as genuinely frontier-class against OpenAI, Anthropic and Google.
tech_top.pm_note: If Meta's frontier model is priced and capable enough to be a real alternative, that's a new negotiating lever worth testing before your next model-vendor renewal.

tech_top.headline: Microsoft's Brad Smith Says the UK Is Best Placed to Lead on AI Regulation
tech_top.blurb: Microsoft president Brad Smith argued the UK is well positioned to set global AI safety rules, floating proposals like tamper-proof logs, independent audits, and a legal duty for organizations to disclose when a rogue AI agent breaches their systems.
tech_top.pm_note: A major vendor publicly courting a specific regulator is worth watching — rules written with heavy vendor input tend to become the compliance baseline everyone else has to meet.

tech_more.headline: Cloudflare Acquires Deno to Improve Its Workers Programming Model
tech_more.blurb: Cloudflare is acquiring Deno, the startup behind the JavaScript runtime of the same name, to strengthen the programming model behind its Workers edge-computing platform; financial terms weren't disclosed.

tech_101.text: When competing businesses coordinate to refuse dealing with a third party — the legal theory DOJ is testing against five rival TV networks that briefly, and jointly, stopped covering White House pool events together.

Industry shorthand for an AI model at or near the current capability ceiling, regardless of maker. Meta calling Muse Wonder 'frontier' is a claim about where it ranks against OpenAI, Anthropic and Google, not just a product name.

science.headline: A Hidden 'Local pH' Factor Can Make or Break a Chemical Reaction
science.blurb: Seoul National University researchers identified local pH — the acidity right at an electrode's surface — as an overlooked variable that decides whether an electrochemical reaction succeeds, and used that insight to raise a target compound's yield from about 16% to 97%. The process builds compounds for plastics, medicines and adhesives using oxygen and electricity instead of a separate peroxide oxidant.

science.headline: MIT Astronomers Catch a Star Feeding on a Brown Dwarf, a Meal That Could Last Billions of Years
science.blurb: Astronomers found a low-mass star about 300 light-years away, ZTF J0440+2325, steadily drawing material from a companion brown dwarf it orbits every 86.65 minutes, the first system observed in this kind of slow stellar feeding. Rather than consuming its partner in one burst, the star is expected to keep siphoning material for billions of years.

philosophy.headline: You're a Christian and a Buddhist (Whether You Like It or Not)
philosophy.blurb: Jonny Thomson's Mini Philosophy column takes up orthopraxy, the idea that religions are better defined by shared practice than by shared belief, drawing on an interview with Andrew Henry to argue that what people do together often matters more than what they privately affirm.

philosophy.headline: 9/11 and the Genealogy of Conspiracy Theories
philosophy.blurb: Andrew McKenzie-McHarg traces how conspiracy theories about 9/11 fit a longer history of apocalyptic thinking, and argues the question of when to take such theories seriously isn't settled by dismissing them outright but by weighing them as one would any claim in a criminal or journalistic investigation.

philosophy_101.text: The view that a tradition is defined by its shared practices rather than its shared beliefs — the lens Jonny Thomson uses to argue most people are, religiously speaking, more mixed than they think.

Reasoning from the available evidence to whichever explanation accounts for it most plausibly — the standard McKenzie-McHarg argues should separate a conspiracy theory worth investigating from one that's pure apocalyptic fantasy.
